chunks: And with the first chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man, from Ibn Muskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Saeed al-Zuhri, from one of the two (Imams), peace be upon them, who said:
Woe to a people who do not make it their religion to enjoin good and forbid evil.
And he said: Whoever professes ‘there is no god but Allah,’ his utterance shall never enter the kingdom of Heaven until he completes it with a righteous deed.
And there is no religion for whoever worships Allah while strengthening falsehood, and there is no religion for whoever worships Allah through obedience to the tyrant.
Then he said: And every community has been distracted by rivalry for worldly abundance, until they visited the graves.

key_terms.التَّكَاثُرُ: Rivalry for abundance (al-takathur) — from Surah al-Takathur (102:1), referring to worldly competition that distracts from the Hereafter
key_terms.النَّهْيِ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ: Forbidding the evil (al-nahy ‘an al-munkar) — the complementary duty to prevent and condemn wrongdoing
key_terms.الْأَمْرِ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ: Enjoining the good (al-amr bi-l-ma‘ruf) — a fundamental Islamic duty to actively promote righteousness
key_terms.مَلَكُوتَ السَّمَاءِ: The kingdom of Heaven (malakut al-sama’) — the celestial realm, entry into which requires action alongside faith

ai.seo_question: What does Islam teach about the relationship between faith, action, and opposing tyranny?
ai.summary: This hadith from one of the two Imams (al-Baqir or al-Sadiq) emphasizes three interrelated principles: the religious obligation of enjoining good and forbidding evil, the insufficiency of mere verbal profession of faith without righteous action, and the invalidity of worship that coexists with supporting falsehood or obeying tyrants. The Imam concludes by citing Quran 102:1-2 as a warning against worldly distraction.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 7. And wilt the preceding chains of narration from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from ‘Ali ibn Hadeed, from ‘Ali ibn al-Nu’man, from Ibn Maskan, from Dawood ibn Farqad, from Abu Saeed al-Zohari, from one the two (Imams), peace be upon them, who said:
"Woe to the people who do not make it their habit to enjoy good and forbid evil."

And then he said: "Whoever professes ’there is no God but Allah, his utterance does not enter the kingdom of Heaven, till it is supplemented by one good deed. And he who seeks to be godly while lending strength to the untruth, such a man has no religion. Similarly, he who is subservient to a tyrant, has no religion."
Then he said: "Every community has been distracted by rivalry for worldly gain and abundance, till they visited the graves."
